about: The code examples of the chapter 14 deck, in the order of the code slides (order = slide order). The page's chapter-code tab lists them by NAME in this order; every example is self-contained, uses openpyxl and the Python standard library only, builds its workbooks in memory (io.BytesIO) instead of in files, opens no network connection, reads no keyboard and opens no window; the chapter's three Excel files (example3.xlsx, censuspopdata.xlsx, produceSales3.xlsx) are replaced by small stand-ins with the same sheets, columns and formulas, named beside the code; the expected result is what the run printed in a fresh interpreter. The code is exactly the text of the deck's code boxes with the '>>> ' prompt removed.

page_requirements: openpyxl 3.1.5 and its one dependency et_xmlfile 2.0.0, which the page embeds as wheels (08-tooling/ch14-page/pywheels_v1_0_0.json) and installs into its browser Python before the first example runs; the standard library modules io, zipfile, datetime, decimal, pprint and sys, and the built-ins print, len, range, enumerate, sorted, list, dict, int, float, type, str, bool, isinstance
No disk file, no subprocess, no keyboard input, no network, no browser window

examples.name: An .xlsx file is a zip of XML parts
examples.code:
import io, zipfile, openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
buf = io.BytesIO()
wb.save(buf)
names = sorted(zipfile.ZipFile(buf).namelist())
print(len(names), 'parts in the zip')
for name in names: print(name)

examples.name: Read-only mode and iter_rows
examples.code:
import io, openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active
for i in range(1, 6): ws.append([i, i * 10])
buf = io.BytesIO(); ws.parent.save(buf)
fast = openpyxl.load_workbook(buf, read_only=True)
sheet = fast.active
print(type(sheet).__name__, sheet.max_row)
rows = list(sheet.iter_rows(min_row=2, max_row=4, values_only=True))
print(rows)

import openpyxl
sheet = openpyxl.Workbook().active
sheet.append(['CensusTract', 'State', 'County', 'POP2010'])

          ('02020000200', 'AK', 'Anchorage', 3040),

examples.name: Project 9: tally tracts and population by county
concepts: Project 9: Reading Data from a Spreadsheet
examples.code:
rows = [('AK', 'Anchorage', 4115), ('AK', 'Anchorage', 3040),
        ('AL', 'Autauga', 1912), ('AL', 'Autauga', 2170)]
county_data = {}
for state, county, pop in rows:
    county_data.setdefault(state, {})
    county_data[state].setdefault(county, {'tracts': 0, 'pop': 0})
    county_data[state][county]['tracts'] += 1
    county_data[state][county]['pop'] += pop
print(county_data)

examples.name: pprint.pformat writes the result as Python
concepts: Project 9: Reading Data from a Spreadsheet
examples.code:
import pprint
county_data = {'AK': {'Anchorage': {'tracts': 2, 'pop': 7155}},
               'AL': {'Autauga': {'tracts': 2, 'pop': 4082}}}
text = 'allData = ' + pprint.pformat(county_data)
print(text)
ns = {}
exec(text, ns)
print(ns['allData']['AK']['Anchorage']['pop'])

examples.name: Project 10: correct the prices
examples.code:
import openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active
ws.append(['PRODUCE', 'COST PER POUND', 'POUNDS SOLD', 'TOTAL'])
ws.append(['Garlic', 1.19, 10.0, '=ROUND(B2*C2,2)'])
ws.append(['Celery', 3.07, 4.5, '=ROUND(B3*C3,2)'])
updates = {'Garlic': 3.07, 'Celery': 1.19}
for row in range(2, ws.max_row + 1):
    name = ws.cell(row=row, column=1).value
    if name in updates:
        ws.cell(row=row, column=2).value = updates[name]
print([ws.cell(row=r, column=2).value for r in range(2, 4)])

examples.name: Writing a workbook: sheets and save
examples.code:
import io, openpyxl
wb = openpyxl.Workbook()
wb.active.title = 'Spam Bacon Eggs Sheet'
wb['Spam Bacon Eggs Sheet']['A1'] = 'Hello, world!'
wb.create_sheet(index=0, title='First Sheet')
wb.create_sheet(index=2, title='Middle Sheet')
wb.remove(wb['Middle Sheet'])
print(wb.sheetnames)
buf = io.BytesIO(); wb.save(buf)
copy = openpyxl.load_workbook(buf)
print(copy.sheetnames, copy['Spam Bacon Eggs Sheet']['A1'].value)

examples.name: A formula is text; the result is cached
examples.code:
import io, openpyxl
ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active
ws['A1'], ws['A2'] = 200, 300
ws['A3'] = '=SUM(A1:A2)'
print(ws['A3'].value, ws['A3'].data_type)
buf = io.BytesIO(); ws.parent.save(buf)
kept = openpyxl.load_workbook(buf)['Sheet']
cached = openpyxl.load_workbook(buf, data_only=True)['Sheet']
print(kept['A3'].value, '|', cached['A3'].value)

examples.name: ROUND in a spreadsheet and round in Python
examples.code:
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP
for text in ('0.125', '1.005', '2.675', '65.205'):
    x = float(text)
    up = Decimal(text).quantize(Decimal('0.01'), ROUND_HALF_UP)
    print(text, round(x, 2), up)

ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active

examples.name: A bar chart: Reference, Series, BarChart
examples.code:
import openpyxl
from openpyxl.chart import BarChart, Reference, Series
ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active
for i in range(1, 11): ws['A%d' % i] = i * i
ref = Reference(ws, 1, 1, 1, 10)
series = Series(ref, title='First series')
chart = BarChart()
chart.title = 'My Chart'
chart.append(series)
ws.add_chart(chart, 'C2')
print(ref, len(ws._charts))

examples.name: A chart is stored as XML in the zip
examples.code:
import io, zipfile, openpyxl
from openpyxl.chart import BarChart, Reference
ws = openpyxl.Workbook().active
for v in (1, 4, 9): ws.append([v])
chart = BarChart(); chart.add_data(Reference(ws, 1, 1, 1, 3))
ws.add_chart(chart, 'C2')
buf = io.BytesIO(); ws.parent.save(buf)
names = sorted(zipfile.ZipFile(buf).namelist())
print([n for n in names if 'chart' in n or 'drawing' in n])
